final_task_tree.title: Figure out a training plan for my dog
final_task_tree.description:
Rescue border collie mix, 14 months. Pulls hard on the leash and barks at every other dog on walks. South Bay, California; I can do evenings and weekends.

Three things only:
1. Whether to hire a trainer or do it myself.
2. If hiring — two or three local options with real prices.
3. A week-by-week plan for the first four weeks.

Don't research anything beyond those three.

subtasks.title: Decide: hire a trainer vs. DIY for leash pulling + dog reactivity
subtasks.description: Question 1 of the brief. Establish what leash reactivity (barking/lunging at other dogs) actually requires, and whether a 14-month rescue border collie mix with pulling + reactivity is a DIY case or a professional case. Deliverable: a clear recommendation with the reasoning and the specific red flags that would push it one way or the other. Note: reactivity is different from aggression — the distinction matters for the answer.

subtasks.title: Find 3 South Bay trainers with real published prices
subtasks.description: Question 2 of the brief. Find 2-3 trainers serving the South Bay (San Jose / Sunnyvale / Santa Clara / Mountain View / Campbell area) who: (a) use positive reinforcement / LIMA methods, (b) explicitly handle leash reactivity toward other dogs, (c) have actual dollar prices, not 'contact us'. Must offer evenings or weekends. Record price, format (private/board/class), credentials, phone, and booking URL in the subtask description.

subtasks.title: Write the week-by-week plan for weeks 1-4
subtasks.description: Question 3 of the brief. A concrete 4-week protocol the owner can run on evenings and weekends, covering both problems: loose-leash walking and dog-dog reactivity. Must specify what to do each week, how long each session is, and what 'working' looks like so they know if it's failing. Should be usable whether or not they hire a trainer.
